sentences.text: ORAL ORDER

The petitioners are before this Court calling in question registration of a crime in Crime No.122/2023, pending before the 3rd JMFC Court, Mangaluru, for the offences under Sections 498A, 504, 323, 506 and 34 of the IPC.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 in unison submit that the parties to the lis have settled their dispute among themselves.
The parties to the lis have decided to obtain a decree of divorce by mutual consent before the concerned Court.
The parties have parted their ways and filed a memorandum of understanding before this Court, by drawing up certain terms and conditions.
One of the conditions of the settlement also recognizes the closure of the present proceedings.
They have also filed an application under Section 320(2) of the Cr.P.C. along with a joint memo and affidavit before this Court to that effect.

The memorandum of agreement reads as follows:
"c) That the gold ornaments like one chain and finger ring gifted by the respondent to the petitioner is agreed to be returned to the respondent and the same shall be handed over to the respondent before the open court on the date of acceptance of this report by the Honourable Court.

d) That the respondent shall withdraw/compromise the case filed by her against the petitioner and his family member for the offence punishable under Section 498A,
323, 504, 506 r/w Section 34 of IPC as per the crime no.122/2023 of Mangalore Women P.S which is pending on the file of the JMFC 3Rd Court, at Mangalore which is now subject matter of Criminal Petition as per the Criminal Petition No.13805/2023 before the Honourable High Court of Karnataka.
In view of the settlement the respondent shall co-operate for the closure of the said petition.
That even otherwise this compromise agreement is itself is a consent of the respondent for closure of the said criminal case or setting aside the said FIR.

e) It is mutually agreed that the respondent has no claim for past, present or future against the petitioner either by way of maintenance/ compensation /alimony/properties etc and petitioner has no claim for past, present or future against the respondent.

f) It is further agreed that the Petitioner will have no right to lay any claim,
Mr Ranjith Bangera @ Ranjith vs State Of Karnataka on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52212225/
3 whatsoever, on the person or any property of Respondent.

entities.text: Ranjith Bangera @ Ranjith vs State Of Karnataka on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Likewise the Respondent shall have no claims of whatsoever nature over person or property of the Petitioner hence forth.
That both the parties shall not have any claims of whatsoever nature against each other.

g) The parties having mutually settled all monetary and other matters of common concern and they have no outstanding issues inter se, they place on record that they have discharged and do hereby release one another of all inter se claims past, present and future."

Though the offences alleged against the petitioners in the case at hand inter alia is one punishable under Section 498A of the IPC, since it is a marital dispute between the husband and wife and now, they have arrived at settlement and parted their ways, I deem it appropriate to accept the memorandum of agreement, joint memo and the affidavit and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, as the allegations are not against the State.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The criminal petition is disposed.
(ii) The Crime No.122/2023, pending before the 3rd JMFC Court, Mangaluru, stands quashed.
